title: Practice Q05: scaling, reversing and states

beats.text: Practice question Q zero five, worth five marks, puts scaling, reversing and states together. Pause the video and attempt all three parts.

Part a. Decomposing one mole of liquid water means reversing the equation and halving it. Reversing flips the sign; halving halves the value. So liquid water forms hydrogen gas plus half a mole of oxygen gas, with delta H equal to positive two hundred and eighty-six kilojoules.

Part b. The negative five hundred and seventy-two refers to two moles of hydrogen, so one mole of hydrogen releases two hundred and eighty-six kilojoules. Zero point seven five zero moles therefore releases zero point seven five zero times two hundred and eighty-six, which is two hundred and fourteen point five kilojoules, reported as two hundred and fifteen kilojoules released.

Part c. No. If the product were water vapour, the products would sit higher in enthalpy, because vaporisation absorbs energy. So less energy would be released, and a different delta H value would be needed.

Marks: two for the reversed, halved equation with its enthalpy; two for the energy released; one for the state explanation. The tempting error is multiplying zero point seven five zero by five hundred and seventy-two, giving four hundred and twenty-nine kilojoules. That treats the equation's value as if it were per mole of hydrogen. The first wrong step is not asking what amount the delta H refers to.
